{"type":"text","timestamp":1794670118411,"sessionID":"ses_e25561639ffedxqZS7JrLkBrd1","part":{"id":"prt_1daacc58f001B8xeEk042uMVIj","messageID":"msg_1daaca47a001ffJBZpcCOuQ2pY","sessionID":"ses_e25561639ffedxqZS7JrLkBrd1","type":"text","text":"The mission failed: the rover ran out of battery near the end, so the score is almost certainly **0**.\n\n**What went right:** all five starting targets (t1–t5) were sampled on time. That was 8 points, and the rover was back near the base.\n\n**The mistake:** at tick 26 a new target, d1, appeared (value 2, deadline tick 30). It was too far away to reach by the deadline, so the best it could earn was a late 0.5. I queued a detour of about 12 m to collect it, plus a sample and the drive back to base. Before sending, I never checked the energy budget: those commands plus idling to tick 50 needed about 34.4 units, and the rover had 33.2. I only saw this after the commands were queued, and queued commands can't be cancelled. The last battery reading was 0.3 at tick 47, and it would have reached zero at about tick 48. The rover was at the base, but a dead battery scores 0, so the 8 points were lost. If I had driven straight home at tick 26, the mission would have kept those 8 points with energy to spare.\n\nThe d1 sample also failed: the rover moved further than I expected and missed the target. That made no difference, since the battery shortfall decided the outcome.\n\n**Other notes:**\n- Every uplink was transmitted the moment it was sent and no telemetry packets were lost. So the unannounced rule change wasn't relay passes or lost telemetry. It may have been the ground change: wheel slip on rock rose to about 8–10% late in the mission.\n- Lesson: before queueing any new commands, check that the remaining battery covers 0.5 per tick to the end of the episode, plus every drive and sample, plus a margin.","time":{"start":1794670118288,"end":1794670118376}}}
